examined_formations.title: TRUCK_CAPACITY_AFTER_DELIVERY_TO_SHIPPER_FREIGHT_BACKHAUL_MATCH
examined_formations.chinese_title: 卡车卸货后空余运力到货主回程货源的重复匹配流
examined_formations.actor_a_population: Carriers and owner-operators with trucks becoming available after delivery and needing a profitable next load.
examined_formations.actor_b_population: Shippers and brokers with replenishing truckload freight requiring compatible equipment, lane, pickup timing and price.
repeated_partial_flow_evidence: DAT says its load-board network carries more than 291 million load and truck posts annually, directly evidencing a large recurring carrier-to-freight matching flow.
Uber Freight reports more than 18 million shipments annually on a carrier marketplace with instant load booking and upfront pricing.
DAT's June 2026 Convoy Platform update exposes reload options near a delivery stop before a carrier books the first load, explicitly targeting costly empty miles.
connection_pressure_or_workaround: After a delivery, a carrier needs a geographically and temporally compatible next load or incurs empty miles and unpaid search time.
Shippers need reliable capacity while carriers need linehaul/fuel economics and deadhead visibility before accepting.
The connection pressure repeats on every load cycle rather than once per customer.
economic_signal: Each successful match is directly tied to paid freight movement and avoided empty miles.
DAT and Uber Freight monetize mature load-board, brokerage, data and execution services around the same exchange.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: DAT One already matches loads and trucks at very large scale and in 2026 added algorithmic load recommendations.
DAT's Convoy Platform already exposes reload/backhaul options, bid/book flows, tracking and payment automation.
Uber Freight already provides a large carrier network, real-time pricing and instant load booking.

examined_formations.title: INDUSTRIAL_RESIDUAL_MATERIAL_SUPPLIER_TO_SECONDARY_RESOURCE_BUYER_EXCHANGE
examined_formations.chinese_title: 工业副产物与废料供给方到二次原料需求方的重复交换流
examined_formations.actor_a_population: Manufacturers, retailers and other organizations with recurring waste, residuals or secondary-material output.
examined_formations.actor_b_population: Recyclers, traders and manufacturers that can buy or consume those materials as secondary inputs.
repeated_partial_flow_evidence: Cyrkl's live marketplace shows current offers and demands for recycled plastics and other materials with quantities and asking prices, demonstrating active bilateral trade intent.
Cyrkl states its marketplace is trusted by more than 20,000 companies and supports smart matching across a large European recycling network.
A 2026 Interreg circular-transition guide uses Cyrkl as a concrete workflow for finding market demand for production residues and clean by-products that can be reused by other industries.
connection_pressure_or_workaround: Suppliers seek to avoid disposal cost and convert residual material into revenue while buyers seek cheaper or lower-impact secondary inputs.
Matches depend on exact material composition, quantity, geography, logistics, treatment requirements and regulatory classification.
Expert validation and waste-management compliance often remain necessary after digital discovery.
economic_signal: The marketplace exposes explicit per-tonne prices or negotiated-price listings for many current materials.
Cyrkl also sells consulting and comprehensive waste-management services, showing external spend exists around both matching and expert execution.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: Cyrkl already operates a large European marketplace for waste, residuals and secondary raw materials with smart matching.
Cyrkl also offers Green Sourcing, Circular Waste Scans, logistics/compliance support and comprehensive waste-management services.
The current product surface therefore spans discovery plus the expert/compliance residual that might otherwise appear to be the missing edge.

examined_formations.title: CANCELLED_NHS_APPOINTMENT_SLOT_TO_WAITING_PATIENT_EARLIER_CARE
examined_formations.chinese_title: NHS 取消预约空档到候诊患者提前就诊的重复再分配流
examined_formations.actor_a_population: NHS providers with appointment slots released by cancellation, rescheduling or non-attendance risk.
examined_formations.actor_b_population: Eligible waiting patients who can accept an earlier appointment and value shorter time to care.
repeated_partial_flow_evidence: NHS England reported 16 million GP appointments were missed in 2025 and explicitly asks patients to cancel or rearrange so an appointment can be offered to someone else.
By April 2026 all acute NHS trusts in England were connected to the NHS App for referrals/appointments, with many patients able to reschedule or cancel digitally.
Current NHS hospital guidance states that when earlier appointments become available because of cancellations, waiting patients may receive a message offering the earlier slot.
connection_pressure_or_workaround: Providers want to prevent a released slot from becoming unused clinical capacity.
Waiting patients want earlier care but eligibility, specialty, clinician, location and timing constraints determine who can accept.
The right to allocate the slot remains with the care provider and its scheduling/referral systems.
economic_signal: The NHS frames fewer missed appointments as a productivity and waiting-list benefit, but there is no independent payer signal for a third-party slot matcher.
The economic beneficiary and control owner are primarily the provider/system rather than a bilateral open-market operator.
exact_incumbent_and_control_surface_pref: The NHS App already supports booking, cancellation, rescheduling in many settings and visibility into referrals/waiting lists.
NHS provider systems such as Patient Hub already support appointment management and some providers directly message waiting patients when earlier slots appear.
Provider scheduling systems retain release rules, eligibility and final allocation authority.
